precepts.text: The Most High raised up prophets from the sons of Israel; the children of the prophets are the children of Israel.
precepts.point: In thee shall all families of the earth be blessed is not talking about everybody. The children of the prophets and of the covenant are Israel, and Israel would be scattered into all nations of the earth; through Abraham's seed the kindreds of the earth are blessed because scattered Israel gets the chance to repent and return, circumcised or not.

note.label: Genesis 12: The Calling of Abram

precepts.why:
Who are the children of the prophets? “And I raised up of your sons for prophets, and of your young men for Nazarites. Is it not even thus, O ye children of Israel? saith the Lord.”

The Most High raised up prophets from the sons of Israel, so the children of the prophets are the children of Israel. The families of the earth blessed in Abraham are Israel scattered into all nations, getting the chance to repent and return.

precepts.text: The Most High raised up prophets of the sons of Israel; the children of the prophets are Israel.
precepts.point: The reason the oath stood: because Abraham obeyed my voice, and kept my charge, my commandments, my statutes, and my laws.

note.label: Genesis 26: The Wells and the Envy of the Philistines

precepts.why:
Who are the children of the prophets? “I raised up of your sons for prophets, and of your young men for Nazarites. Is it not even thus, O ye children of Israel? saith the Lord.” The prophets were raised up of the sons of Israel, so the children of the prophets are Israel.

That settles who Peter was speaking to when he said, ye are the children of the prophets and of the covenant. The covenant sworn to Abraham and performed unto Isaac, “in thy seed shall all the nations of the earth be blessed”, is Israel’s, scattered into every nation; it does not put everybody in it.

precepts.text: I raised up of your sons for prophets; the prophets come out of the children of Israel, not the nations.
precepts.point: That does not make the other nations prophets. Prophets are raised up of the sons of Israel; the Lord used Balaam for one specific purpose, to show the nations there is nothing they can do against Israel when the Lord is on our side, and to have Moses write it down in a book.

note.label: Numbers 24: A Star out of Jacob and the Latter Days

precepts.why:
“And Balaam lifted up his eyes, and he saw Israel abiding in his tents according to their tribes; and the spirit of God came upon him.” Do not be confused at the spirit of God coming on a man of another nation: all the spirits belong to the Most High, and He can do what He wants with any of them.

That does not make the other nations prophets. “And I raised up of your sons for prophets, and of your young men for Nazarites. Is it not even thus, O ye children of Israel? saith the Lord.” Prophets are raised up of the sons of Israel, not the nations.

The Lord used Balaam for one specific purpose: to show the nations there is nothing they can do against Israel when the Lord is on our side, and to have Moses write it down in a book.

precepts.text: For three transgressions of Israel and for four: they lay themselves down upon clothes laid to pledge by every altar.
precepts.point: The history shows how wicked we were to each other: Israel laid themselves down upon clothes laid to pledge by every altar, stacking up people's raiment like pallets and drinking the wine of the condemned in the house of their god, instead of returning the pledge before the sun went down as righteousness. That is why the Lord was judging us.

note.label: Deuteronomy 24: Divorcement, Pledges, and Mercy to the Poor

precepts.why:
The history shows how wicked we were to each other with this very law. “Thus saith the Lord; For three transgressions of Israel, and for four, I will not turn away the punishment thereof; because they sold the righteous for silver, and the poor for a pair of shoes”. And among the four: “they lay themselves down upon clothes laid to pledge by every altar, and they drink the wine of the condemned in the house of their god.”

Instead of returning the pledge before the sun went down as righteousness, Israel laid themselves down upon clothes laid to pledge by every altar, stacking up people's raiment like pallets, and drinking the wine of the condemned in the house of their god. The poor man was to sleep in his own raiment and bless thee; instead Israel slept on it. That is why the Lord was judging us.

precepts.text: The prophets come out of the nation of Israel and no other, because the Most High is in the midst of Israel and none else and the Bible is given to the Israelites and none else.
precepts.point: The same work goes on today; we fill up the street corners all over the earth bringing forth the glorious gospel of the one true living God and Christ, the prophets He raised up to give warning.

note.label: Jeremiah 44: The Judgment on the Jews Who Fled to Egypt

precepts.why:
The Lord sent “all my servants the prophets, rising early and sending them”, pleading with the Jews in Egypt not to do the abominable thing he hates. Amos shows where those prophets come from: “And I raised up of your sons for prophets, and of your young men for Nazarites. Is it not even thus, O ye children of Israel? saith the Lord.”

The prophets come out of the nation of Israel and no other, because the Most High is in the midst of Israel and none else, and the Bible is given to the Israelites and none else. The same work goes on today: we fill up the street corners all over the earth bringing forth the glorious gospel of the one true living God and Christ, the prophets he raised up of our own sons to give warning.

precepts.text: Some of our people watch for iniquity, hating those that reprove in the gate and turning aside the just for a thing of naught; they will sell us just as Amos says.
precepts.point: They lay themselves down upon clothes laid to pledge by every altar and drink the wine of the condemned in the house of their god.

note.label: Amos 2: Because They Sold the Righteous for Silver

precepts.why:
Israel “sold the righteous for silver, and the poor for a pair of shoes”. That goes into oppression, and Isaiah shows the same men: “all that watch for iniquity are cut off: That make a man an offender for a word, and lay a snare for him that reproveth in the gate, and turn aside the just for a thing of nought.”

Some of our people watch for iniquity, hating those that reprove in the gate and turning aside the just for a thing of naught. Just like in today's time, nobody wants to hear the righteous words of the Most High and keep the commandments; when you bring out the commandments you hear, what, I can't wear pants. They will sell us just as Amos says. But “the terrible one is brought to nought, and the scorner is consumed”.

precepts.text: The nakedness of thy father's wife thou shalt not uncover; you profane the Most High's holy name when you go against this commandment.
precepts.point: They lay themselves down upon clothes laid to pledge by every altar and drink the wine of the condemned in the house of their god.

note.label: Amos 2: Because They Sold the Righteous for Silver

precepts.why:
“a man and his father will go in unto the same maid, to profane my holy name”. The law says, “The nakedness of thy father’s wife shalt thou not uncover: it is thy father’s nakedness.” You profane the Most High's holy name when you go against this commandment.

There were men even in that time going in unto their father's wife, and you may find a TV show today promoting that behavior.

precepts.text: The prophets and Nazarites were raised up of the children of Israel, so the "children of the prophets" are Israel.
precepts.point: The purpose is that the blessing of Abraham might come on the Gentiles, the northern tribes, through Christ, who redeemed the twelve tribes from the curse of the law given to Israel. "All nations blessed in Abraham" means the tribes within Abraham's seed, not every nation on earth.

note.label: Acts 10: Cornelius and the Northern Kingdom Grafted In

precepts.why:
“And I raised up of your sons for prophets, and of your young men for Nazarites. Is it not even thus, O ye children of Israel? saith the Lord.”

The prophets and Nazarites were raised up of the children of Israel. So when Peter calls them “the children of the prophets”, he is calling them Israel. And “To him give all the prophets witness”: the prophets were Israel's, and their witness was to Israel.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Breakdown Of Revelation 16
